38:17.ar: ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:17.en: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:18.ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ
38:18.en: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise

38:19.en: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him

38:20.ar: وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:20.en: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech

38:21.ar: ۞وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ
38:21.en: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber

38:22.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡهُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
38:22.en: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

38:27.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا بَٰطِلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
38:27.en: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire

38:28.ar: أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلۡفُجَّارِ
38:28.en: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked

38:29.ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ مُبَٰرَكࣱ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:29.en: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect

34:10.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضۡلࣰ اۖ يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيۡرَۖ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلۡحَدِيدَ
34:10.en: And assuredly We gave David grace from Us, (saying): O ye hills and birds, echo his psalms of praise! And We made the iron supple unto him

34:11.ar: أَنِ ٱعۡمَلۡ سَٰبِغَٰتࣲ وَقَدِّرۡ فِي ٱلسَّرۡدِۖ وَٱعۡمَلُواْ صَٰلِحًاۖ إِنِّي بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
34:11.en: Saying: Make thou long coats of mail and measure the links (thereof). And do ye right. Lo! I am Seer of what ye do

2:251.ar: فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُۥدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُۗ وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضࣲ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:251.en: So they routed them by Allah's leave and David slew Goliath; and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of that which He willeth. And if Allah had not repelled some men by others the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is a Lord of Kindness to (His) creatures

12:53.ar: ۞وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفۡسِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفۡسَ لَأَمَّارَةُۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّيٓۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
12:53.en: I do not exculpate myself. Lo! the (human) soul enjoineth unto evil, save that whereon my Lord hath mercy. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful

48:1.ar: إِنَّا فَتَحۡنَا لَكَ فَتۡحࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
48:1.en: Lo! We have given thee (O Muhammad) a signal victory

48:2.ar: لِّيَغۡفِرَ لَكَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنۢبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ وَيُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡكَ وَيَهۡدِيَكَ صِرَٰطࣰ ا مُّسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا
48:2.en: That Allah may forgive thee of thy sin that which is past and that which is to come, and may perfect His favour unto thee, and may guide thee on a right path

80:2.en: Because the blind man came unto him

80:3.en: What could inform thee but that he might grow (in grace)

80:4.en: Or take heed and so the reminder might avail him

80:5.en: As for him who thinketh himself independent

80:7.en: Yet it is not thy concern if he grow not (in grace)

80:8.en: But as for him who cometh unto thee with earnest purpose

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

6:94.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جِئۡتُمُونَا فُرَٰدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَتَرَكۡتُم مَّا خَوَّلۡنَٰكُمۡ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِكُمۡۖ وَمَا نَرَىٰ مَعَكُمۡ شُفَعَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فِيكُمۡ شُرَكَٰٓؤُاْۚ لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَضَلَّ عَنكُم مَّا كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
6:94.en: Now have ye come unto Us solitary as We did create you at the first, and ye have left behind you all that We bestowed upon you, and We behold not with you those your intercessors, of whom ye claimed that they possessed a share in you. Now is the bond between you severed, and that which ye presumed hath failed you

2:138.ar: صِبۡغَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ صِبۡغَةࣰۖ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ عَٰبِدُونَ
2:138.en: (We take our) colour from Allah, and who is better than Allah at colouring. We are His worshippers

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

68OdDou02RE.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Sad, Dawud's Repentance and the Meaning of Khilafah (38:17-26)
68OdDou02RE.one_line: Dawud repents without excuses, then is named khalifah: stewardship stands on holding to truth and resisting desire, while remembering the Reckoning.
68OdDou02RE.summary: Returning to the Dawud story, he recaps how Surat Sad presents obedience as returning to the truth, which requires that truth be your real concern. Dawud held every role a person can hold, yet when two intruders provoked him during his private worship he ruled after hearing only one side, and the moment he suspected his error he sought forgiveness, offering none of the hundred excuses available to him. We do the opposite: we justify ourselves by pointing at others' faults. He insists religion exists to reform yourself, not others; advice is for those who accept it, and 'I cannot stay silent about the truth' is often a cover for rudeness. Allah's words 'So We forgave him' show it truly was a sin, and the Prophet was corrected for a frown in 'Abasa, so we should fear how we will be judged. Verse 26 is the first time the companions heard the word khalifah, given to Dawud because he fulfilled it. Stewardship means responsibility that grows with ability and rests on two pillars: judge by the truth and do not follow desire, which misguides even people who pray and fast. Those who stray 'forgot the Day of Reckoning': they know it but live as if they did not.

outline.heading: Opening
Each surah from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar looks at obedience from a new angle
outline.gist: Obedience under hardship (Al-Ahzab), societies (Saba), knowledge and resolve (Fatir), life of the soul (Yasin), obeying without seeing the wisdom (As-Saffat).

outline.heading: No obedience without seeking the truth
outline.gist: Sad teaches obedience through returning to the truth, which only happens when truth is the centre of your concern; every story in it illustrates this.

outline.heading: A prophet's story beginning mid-verse
outline.gist: Unlike other prophets' stories, Dawud's starts in the middle of a verse to bind it to the opening; recitation should still start at the verse's beginning.

outline.heading: Awwab: returning before distance grows
outline.gist: The awwab notices a small drift and returns quickly rather than letting a year pass far from Allah; creation returned to Dawud as he returned to Allah.

outline.heading: Decisive speech: defining what cannot be conceded
outline.gist: A leader names the non-negotiables; today people concede matters of indecency and normalisation with an occupier of holy land.

outline.heading: Adam gives forty years of his life to Dawud
outline.gist: Seeing the light between Dawud's eyes among his descendants, Adam gave him forty years, then objected at death; even Adam saw Dawud as special.

outline.heading: Dawud held almost every human role
outline.gist: Prophet with a scripture, king, commander against Jalut, judge, ironworker and inventor, artist with a beautiful voice, father and husband.

outline.heading: His hour of worship and the intrusion
outline.gist: He took time for worship, not rest; two men climbed the wall and entered without permission.

outline.heading: A provocation by design
outline.gist: The two were angels sent to provoke him; their tone was deliberately insolent, yet Dawud stayed courteous and heard them.

outline.heading: Rejecting the Israelite slander; Dawud's ruling
outline.gist: The tale of Dawud coveting a soldier's wife is baseless; read the story at face value. Dawud ruled and added advice about partners.

outline.heading: The mistake: not hearing the other party
outline.gist: He judged without hearing the second side; Shurayh told a caliph to wait, since the other man might have lost both eyes.

outline.heading: Human nature hunts for excuses
outline.gist: When we err we look for ways to reduce blame, especially if the other side erred first; Dawud had a hundred excuses and used none.

outline.heading: He repented without arguing
outline.gist: He did not justify, protest or mention their faults; he sought forgiveness, bowed and returned at once.

outline.heading: A Muslim is busy with his own mistakes
outline.gist: Even if the other side erred a million times, you will be asked about the one mistake you made.

outline.heading: Advice is only for those who accept it
outline.gist: You have no right to force advice on someone who refuses it; your task is to accept advice yourself.

outline.heading: 'I cannot stay silent about the truth' is often rudeness
outline.gist: Everyone can stay silent and often does; the urge to expose others feeds the ego. Islam is about training yourself.

outline.heading: Istighfar means focusing on yourself
outline.gist: Dawud's forgiveness-seeking was about his own part; whether others repent is not your business.

outline.heading: Al-Haddad: moral impurity is like physical impurity
outline.gist: We are disgusted by others' filth but not our own; the saved person sees his own moral filth and overlooks others'.

outline.heading: 'So We forgave him': it really was a sin
outline.gist: Allah forgives only sins; prophets are protected in conveying the message but can commit lesser faults, and their faults would be good deeds for us.

outline.heading: Prophets' sensitivity to sin
outline.gist: A prophet feels guilt over imperfect focus in Fajr, while we are pleased just to have attended.

outline.heading: 'He frowned': the Prophet corrected for a frown
outline.gist: Busy with a Qurayshi leader, he frowned at the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who could not see it, yet a surah was revealed about it.

outline.heading: What if we are judged as the prophets are?
outline.gist: Nothing proves we will be held to a lighter standard; think how often you stayed in the wrong because the other was worse.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 26-29
outline.gist: Reading through 'a blessed Book that they may reflect', with the merged ta' in yaddabbaru and Abu Ja'far's reading.

outline.heading: The first time the companions heard 'khalifah'
outline.gist: In order of revelation this word first came here, applied to Dawud, who embodied it.

outline.heading: Khalifah: acting by His command, not in His absence
outline.gist: A steward carries out a task according to Allah's command; people succeed one another in it.

outline.heading: Every one of you is a shepherd: responsibility grows with ability
outline.gist: The weak answer only for themselves; as you gain strength, wealth and knowledge you answer for siblings, parents, spouse, relatives and society.

outline.heading: Dawud earned the title through mastery
outline.gist: He worked hard, mastered many fields and so was fit to be the Quran's model khalifah.

outline.heading: First pillar: judge by the truth
outline.gist: He repented on mere likelihood of error, not certainty; it was easy for him because he understood stewardship.

outline.heading: The difference is what we care about
outline.gist: We care about our ego, reputation and winning; Dawud cared only where the truth was.

outline.heading: If each fixed himself the world would be fixed
outline.gist: Marriage, schools and dealings would be set right; each of us stands alone before Allah and is asked about himself.

outline.heading: Second pillar: do not follow desire
outline.gist: The nafs never advises good; it seeks only itself. Mercy in the heart comes from the soul, not the nafs.

outline.heading: Fitrah is not the desires of the self
outline.gist: Fitrah is what the soul was created with; he defers a fuller explanation to Surat Az-Zumar.

outline.heading: Desire misguides even those who pray and fast
outline.gist: Outward practice is one thing; inner sincerity and freedom from pride, envy and showing off is another.

outline.heading: Only Allah can see whether you followed desire
outline.gist: You can always argue you followed the truth; desire is hidden, so watch it yourself.

outline.heading: 'They forgot the Day of Reckoning': living as if it were not real
outline.gist: Forgetting here is not losing the fact but ignoring its consequences; knowing about the Reckoning differs from letting it shape your conduct.

outline.heading: Outro

Focus on your own mistakes, not the faults of the other party
Offer advice only to those who will accept it, and accept advice yourself
Treat every role you hold as stewardship you will be asked about
Watch your desires and live as someone who expects the Reckoning

59:5.ar: مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَكۡتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخۡزِيَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
59:5.en: Whatsoever palm-trees ye cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's leave, in order that He might confound the evil-livers

59:6.ar: وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡهُمۡ فَمَآ أَوۡجَفۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ خَيۡلࣲ وَلَا رِكَابࣲ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
59:6.en: And that which Allah gave as spoil unto His messenger from them, ye urged not any horse or riding-camel for the sake thereof, but Allah giveth His messenger lordship over whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

59:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

8:41.ar: ۞وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمۡ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
8:41.en: And know that whatever ye take as spoils of war, lo! a fifth thereof is for Allah, and for the messenger and for the kinsman (who hath need) and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in Allah and that which We revealed unto Our slave on the Day of Discrimination, the day when the two armies met. And Allah is Able to do all things

33:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ جَآءَتۡكُمۡ جُنُودࣱ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا وَجُنُودࣰ ا لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
33:9.en: O ye who believe! Remember Allah's favour unto you when there came against you hosts, and We sent against them a great wind and hosts ye could not see. And Allah is ever Seer of what ye do

2:173.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغࣲ وَلَا عَادࣲ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
2:173.en: He hath forbidden you only carrion, and blood, and swineflesh, and that which hath been immolated to (the name of) any other than Allah. But he who is driven by necessity, neither craving nor transgressing, it is no sin for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

TAFF49eaAwI.speaker: adnan
TAFF49eaAwI.speaker_note: Sunday tafseer series in his own voice, continuing Al-Hashr
TAFF49eaAwI.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 2: Verses 5-7
TAFF49eaAwI.one_line: Al-Hashr 5-7: cutting palm trees during the siege, representing the faith, and fay' distributed so wealth does not circulate only among the rich.
TAFF49eaAwI.summary: After reviewing Banu al-Nadir's expulsion for treason, he explains verse 5. Freezing during a winter siege, the Muslims cut a few small palm trees for firewood, against the Prophet's standing orders for armies, and felt they had sinned; their enemies mocked them as hypocrites about corruption on earth. The verse grants permission after the fact, teaching that even necessity requires permission to harm the earth, and that whoever represents the faith is held to a higher standard because their actions reflect on Islam. Verses 6-7 move to fay', wealth gained without fighting. Against the Arabian custom that warriors take all spoils, Allah directs it to the Prophet, his kin, orphans, the needy and the stranded traveller, whom he likens to a refugee. Unusually, the verse states its reason: so that wealth does not circulate only among the rich. He explains why stated reasons matter, since a ruling with no stated reason never lapses, and draws out a principle for an Islamic economic system: it must not be rigged in favour of the wealthy. He contrasts interest, where the lender bears no risk, with interest-free loans and shared-risk partnership, raises the difference between gold-based money and fiat currency, and points to extreme pay gaps and education debt. The command to take what the Prophet gives was revealed because companions objected to this distribution.

outline.heading: Why study and memorise the last four juz
outline.gist: They summarise the Quran's major principles; memorising them slowly over a year or two is achievable.

outline.heading: The cluster of organisation
outline.gist: Late Medinan surahs that organise relationships among individuals and between groups.

outline.heading: Review: treason forfeits citizenship
outline.gist: Banu al-Nadir were expelled for betraying the covenant, not for their faith, and exile spared bloodshed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Banu al-Nadir: a hungry, freezing siege
outline.gist: The defenders had more food; the besieging Muslims suffered cold desert nights.

outline.heading: The Prophet's rules of war and the cut trees
outline.gist: Armies were told not to kill animals needlessly, cut trees, burn land, or harm women, children or worshippers; the Muslims cut a few trees for fire and regretted it.

outline.heading: Lina: small fruitful palms, cut or left by Allah's leave
outline.gist: Whether they cut them or left them, it was with Allah's permission and to disgrace the defiant.

outline.heading: Cutting a green tree needs permission
outline.gist: The companions understood they could not cut green trees without Allah permitting it.

outline.heading: The enemy's taunt
outline.gist: Banu al-Nadir mocked the Muslims for claiming to oppose corruption while cutting a handful of trees.

outline.heading: Your actions represent the faith
outline.gist: Judging a faith by a few acts out of context is unfair, but what is fair and what is real differ, and Muslims do the same to others.

outline.heading: Representatives are held to a higher standard
outline.gist: Like a judge, physician or imam, the Prophet's soldiers were chosen for character and barred from future campaigns after a misdeed.

outline.heading: Respect for the earth even in necessity
outline.gist: Even freezing soldiers needed permission to cut trees, a strong statement of environmental value.

outline.heading: An incident in the Quran becomes a principle
outline.gist: Few events entered the Quran; those that did carry full authenticity and become lasting values.

outline.heading: Interlude
With 'wa' and without: incident then general rule
outline.gist: When two similar verses differ by a conjunction, the first comments on an incident and the second states the rule.

outline.heading: Fay' versus ghanimah
outline.gist: Ghanimah comes through combat with a fifth to the leader; fay' comes without fighting, as with Banu al-Nadir.

outline.heading: Arabian custom: warriors take everything
outline.gist: Every spoils ruling in the Quran met resistance because it overturned this norm.

outline.heading: 'You spurred neither horse nor camel'
outline.gist: Awjafa is the command for a horse to charge; Arabic's rich vocabulary for horses and camels shows the precision; they did no fighting.

outline.heading: Allah gives His messengers authority over whom He wills
outline.gist: Terror ended this siege, as the wind ended the Siege of the Trench; many wars end without combat.

outline.heading: The general rule for fay'
outline.gist: Whatever is gained without bloodshed from surrounding towns goes to Allah and His Messenger and the listed groups.

outline.heading: The Prophet's kin
outline.gist: His family always took the hardest roles and could not receive charity, so a share compensated them.

outline.heading: Closest first; the traveller as refugee
outline.gist: Spending starts with those nearest; ibn al-sabil, stranded with nowhere to go, matches today's refugee.

outline.heading: Monotheism was easy; the rulings were the hard sell
outline.gist: Arabs resisted Islam less for its theology than for rulings that broke their customs.

outline.heading: 'So that it does not circulate among the rich'
outline.gist: Dulah is something passed around within a small circle, like a cup that never leaves the group.

outline.heading: Rulings with and without stated reasons
outline.gist: Allah usually gives benefits, not reasons; an unstated reason, as with pork, means the ruling never lapses whatever the scenario.

outline.heading: A stated reason bounds the ruling
outline.gist: Here Allah names the reason, which grounds the Islamic financial system.

outline.heading: The system must not be rigged
outline.gist: Islam does not aim to impoverish the rich, but the poor must be able to rise at the pace the rich grow; today's system is rigged.

outline.heading: Interest puts all the risk on the borrower
outline.gist: The lender holds the money and none of the risk, so probability favours him almost every time.

outline.heading: Usury as the main source of slavery in Arabia
outline.gist: Unpayable debts led to people being owned; necessity can allow some flexibility today.

outline.heading: Alternatives: interest-free loans and shared risk
outline.gist: A lender who waits, or an investor who shares the risk, levels the field between capital and labour.

outline.heading: Riba then and fiat currency now
outline.gist: Gold held its value while modern currency loses it by design; he invites further study without claiming specialist authority.

outline.heading: Wealth must be pumped out to the public
outline.gist: Rigged systems historically produced slavery or tiered citizenship, and today's version is only better camouflaged.

outline.heading: A footballer's week versus a family's year
outline.gist: A young player earns weekly more than he and his father earn yearly, while teachers, doctors and builders struggle.

outline.heading: Debt and the devaluing of education
outline.gist: Years of study ending in debt and modest pay make it hard to encourage learning, though knowledge should be valued for itself.

outline.heading: 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it'
outline.gist: Often quoted out of context, it was revealed because companions objected to the distribution; the closing warning is a firm threat.

outline.heading: No Islamic system can be rigged
outline.gist: The wealthy must accept wealth flowing out; he expects future wars over concentrated wealth.

outline.heading: When people have nothing left to lose
outline.gist: Extreme imbalance leads to chaos, as end-time descriptions of raiding suggest.

outline.heading: Organisation with traitors, the earth and wealth
outline.gist: The surah has organised relations with traitors, the environment and the financial system; the poor come next.

2:74.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡمَآءُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَهۡبِطُ مِنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:74.en: Then, even after that, your hearts were hardened and became as rocks, or worse than rocks, for hardness. For indeed there are rocks from out which rivers gush, and indeed there are rocks which split asunder so that water floweth from them. And indeed there are rocks which fall down for the fear of Allah. Allah is not unaware of what ye do

39:22.ar: أَفَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدۡرَهُۥ لِلۡإِسۡلَٰمِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورࣲ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلۡقَٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
39:22.en: Is he whose bosom Allah hath expanded for Al-Islam, so that he followeth a light from his Lord, (as he who disbelieveth)? Then woe unto those whose hearts are hardened against remembrance of Allah. Such are in plain error

39:23.ar: ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّتَشَٰبِهࣰ ا مَّثَانِيَ تَقۡشَعِرُّ مِنۡهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمۡ وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادٍ
39:23.en: Allah hath (now) revealed the fairest of statements, a Scripture consistent, (wherein promises of reward are) paired (with threats of punishment), whereat doth creep the flesh of those who fear their Lord, so that their flesh and their hearts soften to Allah's reminder. Such is Allah's guidance, wherewith He guideth whom He will. And him whom Allah sendeth astray, for him there is no guide

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

JTQZFHkZyu8.speaker_note: single voice; closes his own summer series on contemporary issues
JTQZFHkZyu8.title: Contemporary Issues: Spiritual Drought
JTQZFHkZyu8.one_line: The final talk of his contemporary issues series: the hardened heart, why spiritual fulfillment is essential, and a deen built on love.
JTQZFHkZyu8.summary: He closes his summer series on contemporary issues, half of which dealt with sexuality and relationships, with what he calls spiritual drought: the hardening of the heart and the inner emptiness that wealth, travel and power cannot fill. Starting from the verse on Bani Israel's hearts becoming harder than rock, he presents the first part of Al-Baqarah as a warning to the nation that inherited their obligation. He contrasts the early Muslims, who found such joy in night prayer and the Quran that little else mattered, with Muslims today who hear the Quran and feel nothing. Verses from Az-Zumar and Al-Hadid describe hearts opened to Islam, skins that shiver at the Quran, and the rebuke to believers whose hearts hardened over time. His first request is simply to admit this is not normal. The hadith of Hanzalah shows that the feeling fluctuates and that its purpose is to fuel the work of daily life; a Muslim cannot walk sixty years without it, like a team with no spirit. In the second khutbah he points to Ramadan as a brief taste of that state, cites Ibn Taymiyyah's inner garden, and insists the deen is built on love, without which worship turns mechanical and is eventually dropped.

outline.heading: Opening
The first juz as a warning to the next in line
outline.gist: The first part of Al-Baqarah moves from Adam, the first steward, to those who failed the same obligation; its long account of Bani Israel's failings is there so Muslims, next in line, do not repeat them.

outline.gist: After every rescue and miracle their hearts hardened like rock or harder, though some rocks gush water and some crumble in awe of Allah.

outline.heading: Half our problems concern sexuality
outline.gist: Half the series dealt with relationships and marriage, a fair picture of an ummah that has lost its compass on these matters, alongside climate change and digital addiction.

outline.heading: Spiritual drought: the hardening of the heart
outline.gist: The early generations barely knew this inner dryness; no wealth, travel or power can fill an empty inside.

outline.heading: Every culture seeks spiritual highs
outline.gist: Across cultures and religions people invent practices to keep the inner life alive; feeling no emptiness at all is an even bigger problem.

outline.heading: Look for your heart in the Quran
outline.gist: A classical scholar's advice: if you cannot find your heart while reading the Quran, you have none, so grieve its absence; he is not here to chastise.

outline.heading: The joy of the people of the night
outline.gist: What the Prophet brought gave the early Muslims a fulfilment that made nothing else matter; night worshippers find more joy than revellers, and if Jannah holds that joy its people are happy indeed.

outline.heading: Hearts opened, skins that shiver
outline.gist: Az-Zumar: the one whose heart Allah opens to Islam is in light, woe to hearts hardened against remembrance; the best speech, consistent and ordered, makes listeners' skins shiver and then soften.

outline.heading: Has the time not come?
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud recalls that only four years into Islam Al-Hadid rebuked them, and they asked each other in shame who was responsible; the verse warns against hardening like earlier scripture-holders.

outline.heading: At least admit it is not normal
outline.gist: Hardened hearts lose the path; if the Quran and talk of Allah bring you no joy or goosebumps, acknowledge that this is a problem and start from there.

outline.heading: Hanzalah: I have become a hypocrite
outline.gist: Hanzalah, a scribe of the revelation, tells Abu Bakr that with the Prophet they almost see Jannah but at home among wives, children and chores it fades, so he must be a hypocrite.

outline.heading: An hour and an hour
outline.gist: The Prophet smiles: if they stayed as they are with him, angels would greet them in the streets; the state is meant to fluctuate.

outline.heading: Spirit fuels the long path
outline.gist: The hour of fulfilment exists to fuel the hour of work; he cannot see how a spiritually dry Muslim walks this path for 60 or 70 years.

outline.heading: A team with no spirit
outline.gist: A team in kit and on time but without spirit wins nothing; the person farthest from Allah is the one with a hardened heart.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ramadan's whiff
outline.gist: Youth will not fully embrace the deen without this; Ramadan is cherished despite hunger and fatigue because it gives a whiff of spiritual fulfilment, and whoever has that lacks nothing.

outline.heading: The garden in my chest
outline.gist: The prison saying ascribed to Ibn Taymiyyah: my garden is in my chest; jail is solitude with Allah, exile is tourism, death is martyrdom.

outline.heading: Your spirit needs nourishment
outline.gist: Islam gave the companions fulfilment from within; a more materialistic era has made us forget that the spirit needs food just as the body does.

outline.heading: This deen is built on love
outline.gist: Love Allah who loves you, His Prophet, His book, His deen, its people and His creation; strip love out and what remains is a mutated ideology.

outline.heading: Without love, worship turns mechanical
outline.gist: Love is not hard to recover if we ask for it and prioritize it; forced worship is either dropped or reduced to mechanical movement, as prayer becomes without fulfilment.

7Q5QAOBqSYA.title: The Truth about Oppression
7Q5QAOBqSYA.one_line: On Truth and Reconciliation Day, he argues that refusing oppression is a core Islamic value and that every Muslim must audit himself for it.
7Q5QAOBqSYA.summary: Prompted by the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation and the month of the Prophet's birth, he argues that Islam rests on three core values, righteousness, justice and incorruptibility, and that the first two are essentially the opposite of oppression, a word the Quran repeats hundreds of times. He dislikes single commemorative days because they let people forget the rest of the year, and says the Prophet is best remembered by holding to what he came to establish. He gathers prophetic warnings: Allah forbade oppression on Himself, oppression becomes darkness on Judgment Day, the dua of the oppressed is answered, and the truly bankrupt are worshippers who wronged others. He recalls a teacher who would not curse oppressors in general in case he was one. Turning to the atrocities against Indigenous peoples, he says oppression outlives its act, harms descendants for generations, and rolls like a wheel until it reaches those who ignored it, as he saw in his own region. Muslims must refuse all oppression without cherry-picking and recognize they are guests on this land. The second khutbah uses the Prophet's last request to settle any wrong and Umar's fear of being questioned to urge constant self-examination.

outline.heading: Opening
Towns destroyed for their wrongdoing
outline.gist: The verse just recited says towns were destroyed when they did wrong, at an appointed time; oppression is spoken of in the Quran 289 times.

outline.heading: Truth and Reconciliation Day and what core values mean
outline.gist: The day given in return for genocide and seized land takes him back to Islam's core values, which are neither rituals nor beliefs.

outline.heading: Islam's three core values
outline.gist: Righteousness, justice and incorruptibility run through the whole Quran, and the first two are simply the opposite of oppression.

outline.heading: Against once-a-year remembrance
outline.gist: Muslims should stand firmly against oppression at every level; a single commemorative day lets people remember once and then forget.

outline.heading: Remember the Prophet by the values he came with
outline.gist: In the month of his birth and death, loving his appearance and manners while turning from what he came to change leaves a gap; remember him by what he made sure we would never forget.

outline.heading: Allah forbade oppression on Himself
outline.gist: The hadith qudsi forbidding oppression among His servants, and the warning that oppression becomes darkness on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The dua of the oppressed
outline.gist: Nothing holds back the dua of the oppressed, even a disbeliever or a sinner, whose sins are his own affair.

outline.heading: The truly bankrupt
outline.gist: The one who brings prayer, fasting and zakat but had cursed, struck and taken from others loses his good deeds to them, takes on their sins and is thrown into the Fire.

outline.heading: A teacher who would not curse oppressors
outline.gist: His teacher would not pray against oppressors in general, fearing he might be one himself, leaving a trail of harm he was too blind to see.

outline.heading: It is hearts that go blind
outline.gist: Al-Hajj describes ruined towns, abandoned wells and lofty palaces; reflection is done with the heart, and it is hearts that go blind when we choose to look away.

outline.heading: No prayer on seized land
outline.gist: The Hanbalis do not accept prayer on land taken unlawfully, and the others say you should not stand there, because oppression is a core issue in the deen, not a secondary one.

outline.heading: What happened to the Indigenous peoples
outline.gist: One of the worst atrocities of recent centuries happened on the land we stand on: millions killed and removed and treated as less than human, answered with one day a year.

outline.heading: Oppression outlives the act
outline.gist: Its harm eats at the oppressed and their descendants for generations, which is why bloodshed is the first matter judged between people.

outline.heading: Oppose oppression wherever it happens
outline.gist: Whether in Palestine or against the Indigenous peoples here, Muslims cannot shelve it; he does not claim to have the answers, but ignoring it is not an option.

outline.heading: The wheel that rolled over his own people
outline.gist: Oppression is a wheel that keeps rolling until it reaches you: his people ignored neighbours suffering on both sides for the fifteen years he lived there, and then no one cared when it reached them.

outline.heading: Refuse all of it, without cherry-picking
outline.gist: Muslims refuse oppression whoever suffers it and whoever commits it, and should respect whose land they stand on.

outline.heading: Guests on a land of others
outline.gist: Being a guest is fine, since we are guests in life anyway; if we forget, it will come around to us or to our children.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's last plea from the minbar
outline.gist: Near the end of his life he invited anyone he had struck, punished or wronged to come and take their right from him without fear of a grudge.

outline.heading: No worship covers a wrong owed
outline.gist: He hoped to meet Allah owing no one; whatever your prayer and achievements, if you oppressed someone you stand there until justice is served.

outline.heading: Make sure you are not part of the problem
outline.gist: Muslims must not only refuse injustice around them but keep asking whether they have harmed or mistreated anyone.

outline.heading: Stand for justice before anything else
outline.gist: Even those hoping to intercede cannot help someone who arrives owing others; with the Prophet's month and Truth and Reconciliation Day, remember that we stand for righteousness and justice first.

outline.heading: Teach your children to refuse injustice
outline.gist: Muslims will oppose injustice to their last breath and raise their children to do the same; this is not extreme but core, and Umar lay awake fearing someone was wronged under his rule.

outline.heading: Umar keeps his son off the council
outline.gist: Umar refused to add his fully qualified son Abdullah to the council choosing the next caliph, so only one of his family would be questioned about oppression.

outline.heading: Outro

vDg_FS6Khj4.title: Contemporary Issues: Digital Addiction
vDg_FS6Khj4.one_line: How gaming and social media are engineered to addict, what it costs young people, four habits to regain control, and the week's tragedies.
vDg_FS6Khj4.summary: Opening with the Quranic image of worldly life as play and crops that yellow and blow away, he continues his series on problems an imam a century ago would never have preached about. Many of them, he argues, come from Muslims consciously putting Islam in the back seat and cherry-picking, and admitting that is the first relief. He then presents statistics on phone checking, screen time and self-reported addiction among teenagers, and the side effects of isolation, anxiety and rage. Using the 1980s collapse of Atari, he explains how the industry recovered by borrowing casino techniques such as variable rewards and loot boxes, and how social media algorithms work the same way, so users are being played rather than playing. The hours lost are enormous: a young man may reach ten thousand hours of gaming by twenty-one, enough to master a skill. He links this to Canadian data on boys falling behind in school. He asks for four things: long breaks, tracking time spent, judging the quality of use, and replacing it with habits that feed the spirit, body and relationships. In the second khutbah he addresses the trial over the Afzal family killing and the disasters in Morocco and Libya, urging care for one's emotions and dua for those suffering, who must know they do not grieve alone.

outline.heading: Opening
Worldly life as play and fading crops
outline.gist: Al-Hadid: a life of instinct and desire is play, adornment and rivalry, like rain-fed crops that turn yellow and blow away; this life is an illusion.

outline.heading: Problems no imam faced a century ago
outline.gist: His contemporary issues series covers relationships, climate change, sexual overexposure and now digital addiction, topics a 1930 imam would have been thought mad to raise.

outline.heading: Left on a clear white path
outline.gist: The Prophet left a path whose night is like its day; only someone who does not want the straight path strays from it.

outline.heading: We put Islam in the back seat
outline.gist: Many of these problems exist because Muslims reduced Islam to a name, Eid and Ramadan feasts, and consciously stopped living the Prophet's legacy.

outline.heading: Admitting it is therapeutic
outline.gist: Everyone, East and West, young and old, has cherry-picked Islam, sometimes citing a YouTube imam; admitting it to yourself brings relief.

outline.heading: Digital addiction by the numbers
outline.gist: Half of teens feel addicted to their phones and 12 percent admit gaming addiction; people check phones 96 times a day, once every ten minutes, with seven hours of daily screen time.

outline.heading: Side effects, and the Atari shock
outline.gist: Isolation, anxiety, depression and rage; in the mid-1980s video game revenue collapsed by 95 percent in two years.

outline.heading: Built like a casino
outline.gist: The industry recovered by borrowing casino techniques: fun failures, variable reinforcement, loot boxes, stage hierarchies and clans to drive marathon play; the game is playing you.

outline.heading: You're not smarter than the algorithm
outline.gist: He is not condemning gaming outright; social media feeds work the same way, mixing in what you do not want so you keep scrolling, and these behaviours are now in the DSM.

outline.heading: 68,000 years of youth
outline.gist: The average gamer is 33, so people in their 50s and 60s game too; one game logged 600 million hours, 68,000 years, in its first month.

outline.heading: Ten thousand hours by 21
outline.gist: By 21 a young man may have spent 10,000 hours gaming, enough to master a language, craft, sport or discipline to the level of writing a book on it.

outline.heading: Designed to work against you
outline.gist: He is not demonizing social media; it is designed to keep you coming back, so anyone who uses it must know how it operates to protect themselves.

outline.heading: Boys falling behind
outline.gist: Canadian boys are less likely to graduate and more likely to drop out; as future breadwinners losing focus to screens, this threatens functioning families.

outline.heading: Take long breaks
outline.gist: Delete the apps for three or four months a year, as he does; after a while you stop picking up the phone and rediscover books.

outline.heading: Monitor the quantity
outline.gist: Take walks and visit people instead; these tools have real benefits, but track how much time they take, and weigh quality even more.

outline.heading: Quality: what is it adding to you?
outline.gist: Ask how each use serves your wellbeing, goals and longevity; gamer thrombosis and gamer rage show something is seriously wrong.

outline.heading: Substitute habits that feed the spirit
outline.gist: Replace screen time with habits that nourish the spirit, which the endless feed slowly starves, along with physical health and relationships.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Afzal family trial
outline.gist: The trial in Windsor over the killing of the Afzal family is hard to hear and recalls one of the most difficult times the city has faced.

outline.heading: Grieve with others, or stay away
outline.gist: If you attend in support, be ready mentally and emotionally, go with friends, make dua, grieve and share your feelings; if you cannot bear it, stay away without guilt.

outline.heading: Morocco and Libya
outline.gist: The earthquake and floods brought back what Syrians saw; such tragedies are a chance to show those grieving that they are not alone.

outline.heading: You do not grieve alone
outline.gist: The ummah shares their pain, grief and fear and stands with them in dua; Allah gives these moments so the community practises standing together.

outline.heading: Outro

59:8.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَيَنصُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
59:8.en: And (it is) for the poor fugitives who have been driven out from their homes and their belongings, who seek bounty from Allah and help Allah and His messenger. They are the loyal

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

59:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلࣰّ ا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
59:10.en: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful

63:7.ar: هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لَا تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّواْۗ وَلِلَّهِ خَزَآئِنُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ
63:7.en: They it is who say: Spend not on behalf of those (who dwell) with Allah's messenger that they may disperse (and go away from you); when Allah's are the treasures of the heavens and the earth; but the hypocrites comprehend not

63:8.ar: يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعۡنَآ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لَيُخۡرِجَنَّ ٱلۡأَعَزُّ مِنۡهَا ٱلۡأَذَلَّۚ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
63:8.en: They say: Surely, if we return to Al-Madinah the mightier will soon drive out the weaker; when might belongeth to Allah and to His messenger and to the believers; but the hypocrites know not

3:169.ar: وَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتَۢاۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يُرۡزَقُونَ
3:169.en: Think not of those, who are slain in the way of Allah, as dead. Nay, they are living. With their Lord they have provision

3:170.ar: فَرِحِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَلۡحَقُواْ بِهِم مِّنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ أَلَّا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
3:170.en: Jubilant (are they) because of that which Allah hath bestowed upon them of His bounty, rejoicing for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind: That there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

MWvGn-1leQA.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 3: Verses 8-9
MWvGn-1leQA.one_line: Al-Hashr 8-9: the Muhajirun who gave up everything, the Ansar who loved and preferred them, and protection from the selfishness of the soul.
MWvGn-1leQA.summary: He recaps how Al-Hashr organises life in a mixed citizenry: treason first, then a financial system that must not let wealth circulate only among the rich, which he links to riba and rigged odds. Verses 8-9 change tone from law to love and ethics, describing how Muslims should treat one another. The Muhajirun were stripped of all they owned, as Suhayb's story shows, and are called truthful because losing everything is the real test. The Ansar settled the home and faith before them, loved the newcomers, felt no resentment at what they were given, and preferred them even in poverty. He makes this concrete with his own failed week hosting a displaced friend in Syria, the Ansar refusing land unless the Muhajirun got the same, and the couple who fed a guest in the dark. The closing phrase on being protected from the soul's greed is his focus: selfishness cannot be removed, only guarded against and redirected toward Paradise, the one thing worth being selfish about, by living selflessly. The three wounded soldiers, Abdullah ibn Amr at Uhud and Amr ibn al-Jamuh show companions who aimed their selfishness at the right target. He asks people to learn the joy of giving time, empathy and knowledge, not only money.

outline.heading: Al-Hashr organises citizenship: treason comes first
outline.gist: The surah organises relations in a mixed society, starting with treason because only treason voids the covenant between citizens.

outline.heading: A financial system that does not rig the odds
outline.gist: Wealth must not circulate only among the rich; riba is the lasting example of a system where one side holds the money and the other carries all the risk, and people care about politics mainly when the economy fails.

outline.heading: Verses on Muslims among themselves: less law, more values
outline.gist: Medina held pagans, People of the Book, hypocrites and several Muslim groups; amid technical verses these three speak of love, empathy and selflessness among Muslims.

outline.heading: Reciting verses 8-9 and a note on the long madd
outline.gist: He recites the passage and explains the hamzah and the run of two-count and four-count elongations.

outline.heading: Verse 8 opens a new paragraph
outline.gist: The lam means 'as for', and attaching this verse grammatically to the previous one is forced; a new topic starts here.

outline.heading: Muhajirun stripped of their wealth: Suhayb al-Rumi
outline.gist: Many emigrants were wealthy in Mecca but left with nothing; Suhayb, a freed man who built a fortune, handed Quraysh his camels and his shirt, and the Prophet met him with news of a winning trade.

outline.heading: Those are the truthful: having nothing to lose
outline.gist: They sought Allah's bounty and pleasure; giving up everything proves sincerity, a Muslim should feel he owns nothing, and the story is far harder than its happy ending makes it look.

outline.heading: The Muhajirun were not one group
outline.gist: Most were from Quraysh, descendants of Ibrahim, but others like Bilal came from entirely different backgrounds.

outline.heading: The Ansar settled the home and faith before them
outline.gist: Tabawwa'u means claiming a spot first; 'before them' means before the emigrants arrived, not that Medina believed earlier than Mecca.

outline.heading: They love those who emigrate to them
outline.gist: Emigration is leaving to seek what you were deprived of, which is the story of most Muslims in Canada.

outline.heading: No discomfort in their chests over what is given
outline.gist: Hajah here is unease or resentment; the Ansar felt none at the homes and support given to newcomers.

outline.heading: Hosting a displaced friend in Syria for one week
outline.gist: When a friend's home in Douma was destroyed in 2013 he hosted the family and found it the hardest, most humbling week of his life, ending with him moving out.

outline.heading: Opening homes to people culturally distant
outline.gist: Quraysh, proud descendants of Ibrahim, and the Qahtani Arabs of Medina shared little beyond language, yet the Ansar shared their homes for life.

outline.heading: Love, not tolerance
outline.gist: The Ansar did not merely accept the emigrants; they competed to host them, which is a far heavier word than tolerating.

outline.heading: Sa'd's offer to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
outline.gist: His Ansari brother offered half of everything; Abd al-Rahman asked only for the market and became the richest man in Medina.

outline.heading: The Ansar refuse land in Bahrain unless the Muhajirun share
outline.gist: Offered land as a reward, the Ansar insisted the emigrants living in their homes receive exactly the same.

outline.heading: Against today's anti-immigrant narrative
outline.gist: Few countries welcome immigrants; the hypocrites spread the same poisonous narrative in Medina, but the Ansar did not.

outline.heading: Ithar: preferring others even in poverty
outline.gist: Ithar is putting another's need before your own; khasasah is poverty itself, having nothing at all.

outline.heading: The Ansari couple who fed a guest in the dark
outline.gist: With Medina's homes full and the Suffah living in the masjid, a man hosted a starving traveller, put his children to sleep hungry and pretended to eat, and Allah was pleased with what they did.

outline.heading: How relationships in a Muslim community should work
outline.gist: Old and new, rich and poor: love one another, feel nothing against those given more, and give even from little.

outline.heading: Shuhh of the soul: selfishness, not just stinginess
outline.gist: Bukhl is reluctance to give; shuhh is self-centredness, feeling you should always receive and never be asked to give.

outline.heading: Protection from selfishness is the recipe for success
outline.gist: This verse ends with success, not truthfulness: the selfishness we let live in our souls is what ruins us.

outline.heading: Be selfish about Paradise, selfless on the way
outline.gist: Humans are built to be selfish; Allah designed the deen so the ultimate selfishness, Jannah, is reached only by serving others.

outline.heading: Protected from it, not rid of it
outline.gist: The verse does not say remove selfishness, because that is impossible; it says be protected from its wrong kind.

outline.heading: The plate exercise with the boys
outline.gist: Whoever pulled the shared plate toward himself ate last; offering what you want when you want it is physically hard.

outline.heading: Three wounded soldiers and the water at Yarmouk
outline.gist: Each passed the water to his brother until all three died without drinking, showing that some do reach complete selflessness.

outline.heading: Trade the joy of receiving for the joy of giving
outline.gist: Giving brings deeper, longer joy and better wellbeing; give time, empathy, experience, knowledge and a listening ear, not only money.

outline.heading: An anthem for Muslims: know when your soul is selfish
outline.gist: A two-year-old's selfishness is cute, a grown man's is not; the instinct exists for survival but must be guarded and redirected.

outline.heading: Jabir and his father draw lots before Uhud
outline.gist: Abdullah ibn Amr would give his son anything of this world but not Paradise; he was martyred, and Allah spoke to him without a veil.

outline.heading: Amr ibn al-Jamuh at Uhud
outline.gist: Exempt because of his lame leg, he insisted on going, ran toward the scent of Paradise and was martyred defending the hill.

outline.heading: Selfishness aimed at the right target
outline.gist: The companions knew what to be selfish about; the third group of Muslims comes next.

38:17.ar: ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:17.en: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:18.ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ
38:18.en: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise

38:19.en: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him

38:20.ar: وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:20.en: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech

38:21.ar: ۞وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ
38:21.en: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber

38:22.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡهُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
38:22.en: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

38:27.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا بَٰطِلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
38:27.en: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire

38:28.ar: أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلۡفُجَّارِ
38:28.en: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked

38:29.ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ مُبَٰرَكࣱ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:29.en: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect

38:30.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لِدَاوُۥدَ سُلَيۡمَٰنَۚ نِعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:30.en: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:31.ar: إِذۡ عُرِضَ عَلَيۡهِ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّٰفِنَٰتُ ٱلۡجِيَادُ
38:31.en: When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers

38:32.ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَحۡبَبۡتُ حُبَّ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ عَن ذِكۡرِ رَبِّي حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتۡ بِٱلۡحِجَابِ
38:32.en: And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world) to the remembrance of my Lord; till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain

38:33.ar: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّۖ فَطَفِقَ مَسۡحَۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَاقِ
38:33.en: (Then he said): Bring them back to me, and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks

38:34.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا سُلَيۡمَٰنَ وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا عَلَىٰ كُرۡسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
38:34.en: And verily We tried Solomon, and set upon his throne a (mere) body. Then did he repent

38:35.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَهَبۡ لِي مُلۡكࣰ ا لَّا يَنۢبَغِي لِأَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
38:35.en: He said: My Lord! Forgive me and bestow on me sovereignty such as shall not belong to any after me. Lo! Thou art the Bestower

38:36.ar: فَسَخَّرۡنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجۡرِي بِأَمۡرِهِۦ رُخَآءً حَيۡثُ أَصَابَ
38:36.en: So We made the wind subservient unto him, setting fair by his command whithersoever he intended

38:37.en: And the unruly, every builder and diver (made We subservient)

38:38.en: And others linked together in chains

38:39.ar: هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمۡنُنۡ أَوۡ أَمۡسِكۡ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
38:39.en: (Saying): This is Our gift, so bestow thou, or withhold, without reckoning

38:40.ar: وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:40.en: And lo! he hath favour with Us, and a happy journey's end

20:108.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلۡأَصۡوَاتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا هَمۡسࣰ ا
20:108.en: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur

20:109.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا
20:109.en: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

35:37.ar: وَهُمۡ يَصۡطَرِخُونَ فِيهَا رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي كُنَّا نَعۡمَلُۚ أَوَلَمۡ نُعَمِّرۡكُم مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ وَجَآءَكُمُ ٱلنَّذِيرُۖ فَذُوقُواْ فَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِن نَّصِيرٍ
35:37.en: And they cry for help there, (saying): Our Lord! Release us; we will do right, not (the wrong) that we used to do. Did not We grant you a life long enough for him who reflected to reflect therein? And the warner came unto you. Now taste (the flavour of your deeds), for evil-doers have no helper

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

100:8.en: And lo! in the love of wealth he is violent

24:61.ar: لَّيۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ حَرَجࣱ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَعۡرَجِ حَرَجࣱ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلۡمَرِيضِ حَرَجࣱ وَلَا عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَن تَأۡكُلُواْ مِنۢ بُيُوتِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ ءَابَآئِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ إِخۡوَٰنِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ أَخَوَٰتِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ أَعۡمَٰمِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ عَمَّٰتِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ أَخۡوَٰلِكُمۡ أَوۡ بُيُوتِ خَٰلَٰتِكُمۡ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكۡتُم مَّفَاتِحَهُۥٓ أَوۡ صَدِيقِكُمۡۚ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَأۡكُلُواْ جَمِيعًا أَوۡ أَشۡتَاتࣰ اۚ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُم بُيُوتࣰ ا فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ تَحِيَّةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُبَٰرَكَةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
24:61.en: No blame is there upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick nor on yourselves if ye eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your fathers' brothers, or the houses of your fathers' sisters, or the houses of your mothers' brothers, or the houses of your mothers' sisters, or (from that) whereof ye hold the keys, or (from the house) of a friend. No sin shall it be for you whether ye eat together or apart. But when ye enter houses, salute one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and sweet. Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations for you, that haply ye may understand

68:51.ar: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزۡلِقُونَكَ بِأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجۡنُونࣱ‏
68:51.en: And lo! those who disbelieve would fain disconcert thee with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: Lo! he is indeed mad

42:49.ar: لِّلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَٰثࣰ ا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ
42:49.en: Unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. He createth what He will. He bestoweth female (offspring) upon whom He will, and bestoweth male (offspring) upon whom He will
